title: SQL Injection and Account Takeover on E-Commerce Platform
summary: A self-initiated responsible disclosure engagement uncovering unauthenticated account takeover (including admin accounts), two independent SQL injection vulnerabilities, and exposure of live third-party credentials across two separate customer databases.

timeline.summary: Authentication flow testing uncovered account-takeover primitive.
Differential testing identified boolean-based blind SQL injection.
UNION-based injection discovered on related endpoint yielding direct data access.
Escalation attempts blocked by database-level privilege restrictions.
Cross-schema enumeration revealed second customer database with live credentials.
Findings compiled; outreach initiated to establish secure disclosure channel.

confidentiality.summary: Unauthenticated read access to full customer PII across two databases, plus administrator credentials and live third-party API secrets.

integrity.summary: Unauthenticated write access to any user's data, including administrator accounts.

availability.summary: No denial-of-service confirmed; data tampering could disrupt order fulfillment.

privacy.summary: Full names, national ID numbers, phone numbers, addresses, and financial data exposed.

regulatory.summary: Exposed data categories fall within scope of national data protection legislation.

operational.summary: Live payment and messaging provider credentials confirmed exposed.

lessons.summary: Never change more than one variable per test window once inside a live chain.
Stop pulling rows the moment a read primitive is proven.
Live, currently-usable credentials are a different risk category from static data exposure.
Admin accounts in same table as users, distinguished only by a flag, amplifies authorization bugs.
Self-initiated disclosure to organizations with no published security contact is materially slower.

seo.description: Case study: responsible disclosure engagement against e-commerce platform, uncovering SQL injection, account takeover, and credential exposure.
